overview.text: On the evening of April 14, 1865, actor and Confederate sympathizer John Wilkes Booth shot President Abraham Lincoln at Ford’s Theatre in Washington, D.C., while Lincoln watched the comedy Our American Cousin. Lincoln was carried across the street to a boarding house and died at 7:22 a.m. the next morning. The attack came just five days after Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered at Appomattox, as Washington celebrated Union victory. Lincoln’s death abruptly turned that celebration into mourning. Booth’s attack was part of a wider plot that also targeted Secretary of State William Seward and Vice President Andrew Johnson, though Johnson was not attacked.

key_facts.text: Booth shot Lincoln during a performance of Our American Cousin at Ford’s Theatre on April 14, 1865.
Lincoln died in the Petersen Boarding House, across the street from the theatre, at 7:22 a.m. on April 15.
Booth had first plotted to kidnap Lincoln; as the Civil War neared its end, he shifted to a plan to murder him and target other leaders.
Lee’s surrender at Appomattox came five days before the assassination; Lincoln’s death halted Washington’s celebrations of Union victory.
Booth escaped after the shooting but was tracked down and killed in Virginia on April 26, 1865.
